title: A DNS Change Is Not Instant Failover
description: A region fails. The team changes its DNS answer to a healthy region, but some clients still contact the old address. What should the disaster-recovery plan account for?

options.text: Resolver and client caching can delay a DNS switch; test that behavior and use a global routing layer when faster failover is required.
options.explanation: DNS steers names, but cached answers and existing connections make failover imprecise. Low TTLs help without guaranteeing immediate migration.

options.text: Changing the authoritative record invalidates every cached answer.
options.explanation: There is no universal push invalidation of DNS caches.

options.text: The new region must use larger JSON responses to refresh DNS.
options.explanation: Payload size has no mechanism to update a client's cached address.

options.text: A TTL of zero guarantees all existing connections move immediately.
options.explanation: DNS TTLs do not migrate established connections, and client behavior still needs testing.
